intent: Fixes 'auto-merged, green, and never deployed'. lifecycle:auto_merge hands the merge to GitHub via the enablePullRequestAutoMerge mutation; GitHub then performs the merge on behalf of whoever ENABLED it. We enabled it with the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub's recursion guard suppresses every workflow trigger for GITHUB_TOKEN actions — so an auto-merged PR fires NO `push` event, a CD workflow on `push: [main]` never runs, and the commit sits on main looking shipped while nothing deployed. OBSERVED DOWNSTREAM (cuspr, 2026-08-02): PRs #416, #417, #418 and #419 all auto-merged on terminal PASS and not one of them triggered a deploy. `gh run list --commit <sha>` returned ZERO runs of any kind for the merge commit. That repo had already recognised the hazard and papered over it with a ten-minute cron safety net, but GitHub throttles scheduled workflows on busy shared runners: every deploy run in the last 12 was `event: schedule`, never `push`, at an observed cadence of 1-3 HOURS (01:16, 04:42, 07:19, 09:26, 10:57, 12:03, 13:48, 14:51, 15:56, 16:54, 17:56, 19:06). So 'merged' and 'deployed' drift apart by hours with nothing anywhere saying so. An earlier incident in the same repo held 29 commits for 5 days (their issue #347). The cron is a mitigation for the symptom; this is the cause. THE FIX: a `merge-token` action input (env PLUMBLINE_MERGE_TOKEN). When set to a PAT or GitHub App token the merge is attributed to a real identity and `push` behaves normally. It falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN so repos that do not deploy on push need no configuration — but the gate now SAYS SO on that path, in both the PR comment (gate.reasons) and the job log, instead of merging silently into a void. Making the fallback loud is half the value here: the bug wasted time because it was invisible, not because it was slow. Token selection is extracted into resolveMergeToken() so both the choice and the suppression flag are unit testable rather than buried in the middle of the run command. Blank and whitespace-only values are treated as absent — an unset action input arrives as the empty string, and passing that as a bearer token would fail the mutation and silently disable auto-merge altogether, turning one quiet failure into another. NOT CHANGED: the gate's verdict logic, the mutation itself, and the GITHUB_TOKEN default. No repo behaviour changes until a repo opts in by setting merge-token. NOTE FOR THE RELEASE: downstream pins the action by tag, so this needs a tag before cuspr can adopt it; tagging is left to the maintainer. PROTECTED SURFACE: YES — this touches action.yml and src/github.ts, both on the mission's protected list, so self_modifying is true and human sign-off is required. That is correct: the change alters how the gate authenticates the merge it performs on a repo's behalf, which is exactly the class of change that should not self-approve.

result_summary: Auto-merged PRs never deployed, and nothing said so. lifecycle:auto_merge enabled GitHub's native auto-merge with the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN actions — so the merge commit fired no `push`, CD on `push: [main]` never ran, and main looked shipped when it was not. Confirmed on cuspr: four auto-merged PRs, zero workflow runs on the merge commit, and 12 straight deploy runs that were all `event: schedule` at a 1-3 hour throttled cadence rather than the ten-minute cron the repo had configured as a safety net. Adds a `merge-token` input so the merge can be attributed to a real identity, keeps GITHUB_TOKEN as the default, and — importantly — makes the fallback warn loudly in the PR comment and the log instead of failing silently. Token selection extracted to resolveMergeToken() for testability, with blank inputs treated as absent so an unset input cannot disable auto-merge outright. New test verified to fail against the old behaviour; 330/330 pass. Needs a tag before downstream can adopt it.
